newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel-PLO summit doubtful on Thursday - official.
newsitem.headline: Israel-PLO summit doubtful on Thursday - official.

text.p: PLO officials said they doubted Palestinian President Yasser Arafat would meet Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Thursday, adding both sides were studying a proposal by Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak for a three-way summit.
"Most probably the meeting will not take place tonight. President Mubarak has proposed a three-way summit in Cairo and both sides are studying it," one of the officials said.
"It has not been settled up until now," Arafat told reporters during a visit to Shifa Hospital in the Gaza Strip.
Another official, Arafat's adviser Nabil Abu Rdainah, told Reuters: "There are attempts to hold summit meetings. This will be decided in the next few hours."
He said Arafat had been contacted by Arab and other world leaders about the clashes across Palestinian areas in which 44 Arabs and 11 Israelis have been killed in two days of clashes.

"The Palestinian position, which is backed by Arabs and the international community, is simple. We are demanding that Israel implements accords, starting with redeployment from Hebron, and to close the tunnel," he said. "This is the only way to save the peace process."
The clashes were triggered by Israel's opening of a tunnel near Islam's third holiest shrine, al-Aqsa mosque.
Palestinians, frustrated at a foundering peace process, assailed the opening of the tunnel as an assault on their holy sites and an attempt to Judaise Jerusalem.

"Benjamin Netanyahu must take a decision to close the tunnel which, among other Israeli policies, led to this huge explosion. This will reduce tension but it is not enough," said Ahmed Tibi, an Israeli Arab and adviser to Arafat.
"The only solution is immediate enforcement of accords, starting with Hebron," he told Reuters.

Palestinian officials said they expected demonstrations in the West Bank and Gaza to continue if Israeli and Palestinian leaders failed to reach a political solution that would advance peace and ease economic hardships.
